newsitem.title: PERU: Peru cenbank sees 5.8 pct/GDP '96 current acct gap.
newsitem.headline: Peru cenbank sees 5.8 pct/GDP '96 current acct gap.

text.p: Peruvian Central Reserve Bank President German Suarez predicted a current account deficit for 1996 equivalent to 5.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), down from 7.2 percent last year, according to government daily El Peruano's Wednesday edition.
The central bank head added that the current account deficit would likely fall further to 5.5 percent next year.
He also predicted a $1.771 billion trade deficit this year -- down sixteen percent from last year's $2.115 billion.
Suarez said exports this year would reach $5.925 billion, with imports of $7.695 billion.
Financial daily Sintesis also quoted Suarez as saying the trade account would be balanced by the year 2003.
